  "summary": "This 22 January 1963 letter from Prof. N. G. Ranga to C. Rajagopalachari (“Rajaji”) reports on parliamentary discussions concerning the Colombo proposals on the Sino-Indian border dispute. Ranga says the Prime Minister had indicated that the government would accept the proposals in principle, while opposition groups—including the PSP, Socialists, Jan Sangh, and Frank Anthony’s independents—had made clear that they could not accept them. Ranga describes a tactical decision not to move an amendment, both to avoid giving the government positive authority for further negotiations and to preserve the November 14 unanimous resolution as a constraint on the government’s position.\n\nThe letter also discusses the Constitution Amendment Bill concerning the DMK. Ranga explains that his party would support the Bill by vote but would not speak in favour of it while Rajaji was questioning the wisdom of introducing it. He says he will open the party’s case on the Colombo proposals and that R. K. Deo will later summarise their position. The accompanying page contains two telegram drafts, addressed respectively to Minoo Masani and Piloo Mody in Bombay and to C. Rajagopalachari in Madras, seeking reactions to a proposed strategy of allowing discussion while offering silent support for the Constitution Bill and opposing “antidisntegration.”",
